extracted.intended_audience: practitioners and students of English patent law (patent attorneys, solicitors, judges) and inventors seeking legal guidance
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and practice for when letters patent are void or voidable under English law, and the procedural steps (scire facias, surrender, chancery/common-law interaction) to have a patent cancelled or defended. Covers substantive grounds of invalidity, defenses that do not vitiate a grant, evidentiary/practice points, and remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer equity (Chancery) proceedings before law suits
rubrics_metrics.description: Before a suit at law, it is often preferable to take proceedings in equity. If the patent is really good, the injunction prevents any further infringement; if it is doubtful, the defendant will be restrained from using it until its validity has been examined. The order for an account puts the patentee in a better situation than if he had to depend upon a jury for damages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equity gives injunctions and accounts and may relax strict rules of law as to evidence; therefore, when a patentee wants injunctions/accounts or indulgence from strict evidentiary rules, it becomes necessary to sue first in Chancery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chancellor's discretion as to reviving injunction after verdict
rubrics_metrics.description: When a verdict has been given and a party moves to revive or make an injunction perpetual, the Lord Chancellor will consider whether, in point of law, he is satisfied that no argument can prevail upon a court of law to have the question reconsidered in a new trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Chancellor thinks a law court might reconsider the validity, he will not revive the injunction but will direct the account to be kept until that motion is made; if convinced the law court will treat the jury verdict as final, he will revive and make the injunction perpetual (3 Meriv. 631 etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents void under Statute of Monopolies: contrary to law or mischievous to the state
rubrics_metrics.description: By the statute of Monopolies (21 Jac. I. c. 3. s. 6) letters patent shall be void altogether or generally if they are (1) contrary to law; or (2) mischievous to the state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mischief may consist in raising the price of commodities at home, being hurtful to trade, or being generally inconvenient. If a patent produces these baneful effects it will be void as a monopoly. Examples and authority (e.g., Darcy v. Allen, Arkwright discussion) are given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mischief categories that can render a patent void
rubrics_metrics.description: The mischief contemplated by the statute may be done by (1) raising the price of commodities at home; (2) being hurtful to trade; or (3) being generally inconvenient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are factual matters that must be pleaded with specificity in record/issue (see Arkwright discussion). A general allegation that a patent is 'prejudicial to the country' is insufficient without stating how.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents voidable for uncertainty, misrecitals, or false suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: All kinds of grants (including patents) may be rendered void for uncertainty, misrecitals, and false suggestions in the grant or specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction of royal grants and prior chapters show that uncertainty/misrecital/false suggestion are substantive defects that can invalidate a patent even if the invention appears new.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent may be void in whole or in part even if invention is new
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent may be void, although the invention be new, either altogether or for something in particular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is possible for novelty to exist but for other legal defects (e.g., monopoly, insufficient specification) to render the patent void as to some claims or entirely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentee must be the true inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: A grant is invalid when the patentee is not the inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof that the grantee was not the true and first inventor is a ground for cancelling the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Object must be a ‘manufacture’ (proper subject matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent is invalid when its object is not a manufacture (i.e., not a proper subject for letters patent for invention).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See earlier chapters for definition; subject-matter defects can render grant void.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification must be sufficiently correct and complete
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent is invalid when the specification is not sufficiently correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insufficiency of specification (failure to describe/enable what is claimed) is a standalone ground to destroy the patent; the patentee must be prepared to defend sufficiency in scire facias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent must be obtained in the usual mode and bear required construction
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent has not been obtained in the usual mode, or will not bear the necessary construction that must be put upon it, it is void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formalities and correct form/process of grant are material; irregular procurement can invalidate the patent (see Chap. V and VI references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Only one sufficient objection needed to cancel the grant
rubrics_metrics.description: Any one of the circumstances appearing in evidence (e.g., non-inventor, bad specification, wrong mode) will be the means of destroying the patent; it is not necessary to prove more than one objection or cause for cancelling the grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plaintiff/attacker need only establish one valid ground of invalidity to succeed in cancelling the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mistakes that do not vitiate a grant (non-vitiating errors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some mistakes do not vitiate a grant: (1) every false recital in a thing not material will not vitiate if the king's intention is manifest; (2) if the king is not deceived in his grant by the party's false suggestion but from his own mistake upon the party's surmise/information, it will not vitiate; (3) if the king is mistaken in law or fact, but that mistake is not part of the consideration of the grant, it will not avoid it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materiality and the monarch's intention/consideration determine whether an error avoids the patent; immaterial recitals or royal mistakes (not induced fraudulently) are generally insufficient to cancel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scire facias available to repeal an invalid patent (who may obtain)
rubrics_metrics.description: The king (by writ of scire facias) may repeal his own grant for the advancement of justice; any subject prejudiced by a grant may petition the king to have it repealed (all persons injured by an illegal patent may petition). Between subjects, the first patentee generally may have scire facias to repeal a second patent, but the second cannot repeal the first by scire facias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standing to seek repeal is broad (king and any injured subject); priority between competing patentees affects who may seek repeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scire facias is an original writ founded on matter of record and issues out of Chancery
rubrics_metrics.description: The scire facias for repeal is an original writ and must be founded on some matter of record. A patent for an invention is a record in Chancery, so the writ must issue out of that court; it is directed to the sheriff and made returnable in the petty bag office; the record of proceedings upon the writ is made up in Chancery and sent into a court of common law to be tried.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural formality: memorial/petition to crown, king's warrant to sue, Attorney-General grants us fiat, summons to defendant, scire facias recites patent and grounds; record then goes to common-law court for trial. See Tidd's Practice and authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and contents of the scire facias pleading
rubrics_metrics.description: The scire facias in form recites the patent and states the grounds upon which it is meant to be impeached (e.g., that the patentee was not the first and true inventor, or that it had been previously invented or used by others).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounds must be particularized in the writ—general, undefined accusations (e.g., 'prejudicial to the country') are improper; issues should state facts to give notice to defendant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pleadings, pleas, and demurrers in scire facias practice
rubrics_metrics.description: After appearance, defendant may plead in abatement or in bar; the most usual defence is the general issue. If matter be insufficient in law upon the face of proceedings, defendant may demur. If demurrer to part and issue on residue, whole record is sent to common law and judgment given on demurrer as well as issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard common-law procedural responses apply; demurrer practice can send legal questions to courts of common law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default judgment and nihil returns
rubrics_metrics.description: If the defendant has been warned and nihil is returned twice, judgment for annulling the patent may be taken by default; judgment may be obtained by confession if no defence is made after appearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to plead or appear leads to annulment by default; procure proper service and returns to obtain default judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence in scire facias similar to infringement trial but burden differs
rubrics_metrics.description: The evidence is similar to that produced upon a trial for infringement; except that the patentee (here defendant) does not need prima facie evidence of novelty and sufficiency of the specification, but must be prepared strongly to rebut every allegation in the writ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attacker must prove allegations in the writ; patentee's defensive burden is to refute allegations; courts may grant new trial only if the case has not had fullest investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity required when alleging public prejudice or inconvenience
rubrics_metrics.description: Issues of inconvenience/prejudice to the public (grounds under the statute) must be stated as particular facts in the record; a general plea that the grant is 'prejudicial and inconvenient to his majesty's subjects' without specifying how is insufficient and may be struck as a surprise to the defendant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pleads must give fair notice so defendant can prepare evidence; courts will not permit undefined 'consequential' issues—state the facts that make it prejudicial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality of judgment in scire facias (no writ of error/appeal)
rubrics_metrics.description: The judgment after trial in scire facias (whether patent revoked or adjudged valid) is final; no writ of error or appeal to another tribunal can be made because of the nature of the proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should seek all defenses at trial; relief by appeal is not available in this form of proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs rule for scire facias repeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Although statute (8 & 9 Will. III. c. 11) gives costs in suits upon writs of scire facias in some cases, because the proceeding to repeal a patent is criminal in its nature that statute does not extend to it; therefore costs are not payable to crown, prosecutor, or defendant on this scire facias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical consequence: parties cannot expect statutory costs in these repeal proceedings; see authorities (The King v. Miles etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Surrender and enrolment required to vacate patent
rubrics_metrics.description: When the patent has been adjudged to be revoked, it must be actually surrendered, cancelled, or vacatur entered on the enrolment of the patent; only after surrender/enrolment is the patent sufficiently cancelled to be of no effect in law. A surrender must be enrolled; certificate should be obtained of the vacatur having been entered on the roll.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative step required after judgment: ensure enrolment of surrender/vacatur and obtain certificate. Note duplicate originals: surrender of original may vacate grant even if duplicate not surrendered.
